scope.question: Is native lexical conditional-prior leakage into constrained generative-recommendation exposure distinct enough to justify D0-D?
scope.evidence_policy: Official proceedings or primary author preprints were used for final evidence; search snippets were discovery aids only.

claim_boundary.allowed: A GRAM-class mechanism claim: frozen pretrained native lexical conditional priors leak through semantic-to-lexical item paths into constrained beam exposure, demonstrated with parent- and popularity-matched controls, followed by a recommendation-specific structured intervention if later supported.
forbidden: first discovery that language models have token or answer priors
first decoding-bias analysis for generative recommendation
first popularity debiasing method for generative recommendation
simple frozen-prior subtraction as a standalone algorithmic novelty claim

verified_claims: Standard length normalization amplifies items containing ghost tokens whose generation probabilities are close to one.
D3 disables length normalization for ghost tokens and uses a text-free assistant model to encourage less frequently generated tokens.
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: Its identified cause is length normalization/ghost tokens and homogeneity, not frozen-base native lexical prior measured on structured lexical item paths under sibling/popularity controls.

verified_claims: Language models can prefer answers common in pretraining data.
A content-free input can estimate answer bias and calibration can make that distribution uniform.
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: This establishes the general prior-estimation/calibration concept, but not Trie-constrained generative recommendation, structured item paths, candidate exposure, or tail miss.

verified_claims: GRAM translates semantic identifiers into the native lexical vocabulary.
The translation is intended to preserve hierarchical and collaborative item relationships.
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: GRAM does not report a frozen-base native-prior audit or neutralization.

verified_claims: Structured Term IDs use standardized textual keywords from the native vocabulary.
The framework addresses semantic gap, hallucination, and item grounding.
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: It does not isolate native-token conditional prior as a source of unequal item exposure.

verified_claims: APAO attributes premature pruning to teacher-forced training versus beam-search inference inconsistency.
It applies prefix-level and worst-prefix optimization.
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: The mechanism is learned prefix vulnerability, not a frozen pretrained lexical prior.

verified_claims: Semantic-ID tree proximity induces correlated item probabilities.
Latte adds latent tokens to form multiple conditioned trees.
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: The mechanism is tree-induced probability coupling; NLPL matches the parent tree before comparing native final-token prior.

verified_claims: Token-Weighted Multi-Target Learning upweights rare tokens under long-tailed item/token distributions.
Ghost attributes popularity bias to token-level optimization and undifferentiated tokenization.
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: Both concern recommendation-data frequency/optimization; NLPL holds training frequency approximately fixed and measures an original pretrained model.

mechanism_isolation.assessment: No audited generative-recommendation work isolates frozen pretrained native lexical conditional prior from learned popularity, tree coupling, and length-normalization effects.

gram_specific_audit.assessment: No audited work performs a parent-matched and popularity-matched lexical-item beam-exposure analysis for semantic-to-lexical recommendation.

intervention_space.assessment: No audited work neutralizes a frozen-base conditional prior at structured lexical-ID path level under Trie-constrained recommendation.
intervention_space.caveat: General content-free prior calibration and recommendation decoding debiasing already exist, so a later method must be recommendation-specific and supported by the proposed mechanism; subtraction alone is not novel.

decision.reason: All three preregistered distinctions survive, but Calibrate Before Use and Decoding Matters rule out broad claims about token priors, content-free calibration, or decoding bias.
decision.allowed_next_action: Implement and run only the preregistered dual-dataset CPU D0-D diagnostic.
